✨ 2025 ✨

What a year.. looking back at the last 365 I am in awe at how many challenges came my way and yet I still chose JOY, peace and love. This year was chaotic but I needed it. I needed it to step into this empowered feminine energy that I now possess boldly. 

I feel so certain of who I am in this moment and I wouldn’t have felt this way if I wasn’t disappointed, hurt, heartbroken, angry, burnt out or exhausted. 

I intentionally spent the year being single to really understand who I am, how I want to be loved and how I want to love but it all had to start with me. Who would I be if I gave myself the love I kept giving elsewhere? ..and BOY, have I loved being on the receiving end. I took myself on dates, I built my relationship with God, I invested in my health, I created a structured routine for myself and I stepped out of my comfort zone. 

My mission was to learn myself outside of my career and although I am still learning, it’s been amazing to realise that I am not defined by my accolades and accomplishments. I am me with or without those things!

I already know that in 2026 I will receive the gifts of the inner work I have done. There will be so many changes, new experiences, healing, joy and growth! I stepped into my fly and I’m never looking back. 

Happy New Year beautiful people! I pray that your year ahead is filled with an abundance of everything you pray for and everything God (whoever/ whatever you believe in) has prepared for you beyond your own dreams. ✨

1. You set the standard for how people treat you and see you. It all starts with how you treat yourself. If you want to be treated with respect then be sure to respect yourself. 

2. If you want to be forgiven, learn to forgive. No-one is perfect. 

3. Even in the midst of chaos, eat and look after yourself. You cannot be at your best if your cup is empty. 

4. Healing is not always going to look and feel pretty. It requires uncomfortable conversations, clearing out the hurt deep within and sitting down with your younger self. Go at your own pace and give yourself grace. 

5. Be kind to yourself, you are not always going to get things right the first time or make everyone happy. Move with positive intention and try your best.

6. Listen to your body, it will tell you to avoid situations/ people or decisions before they occur. Don’t ignore that gut feeling within.

What has been the biggest lesson so far of 2022? Or the toughest pill to swallow? I have an abundance but the one that is most recent is understanding that sometimes when you protect yourself or enforce boundaries, it may hurt someone else. 2022 was a healing and strengthening experience. It was a year for me to look at life from a new perspective not dwelling on what I lost but what I gained. It taught me to keep going, to trust that whatever it happening is always for me, to take accountability, to create boundaries, to learn to say no, to pour into my own cup and to recognise I have done so many incredible things at only 25. I didn’t share the tears, the moments of sadness or loneliness in this video because ultimately; the joy outweighs it. Here are some lessons 2022 taught me. I can only pray that 2023 guides me, nourishes me and fulfils me. ✨ — 

LESSONS FROM 2022. 
People come just as much as they go, you have no possession over anyone. 

You never become “healed”, you just learn how to change the perspective of your pain. 

You can forgive without hearing an apology. 

Sometimes enforcing boundaries will hurt others. But would you rather hurt yourself or another? 

There is no such thing as being the perfect boss, perfect friend, sister, wife etc. Be open to learning, making mistakes and growing. 

Life will feel happy, then sad then happy again. Don’t try to always be one emotion; the goal is to be present.

Sadness isn’t a bad thing.

Rest before your body makes you.

You are not a burden.

Life is what you make it, if you want to be successful focus on your success. If you want to be at peace; focus on your peace.

Ingredients ••
2 red onions
2 red peppers 
3-4 red scotch bonnets 
4 tomatoes 
1 tube of tomato purée 
4 cups of rice 

Seasonings ••
3 Maggie cubes 
1-2 tea spoons of curry powder 
1-2 tea spoons of all purpose seasoning 
3-4 Bay leaves 

Instructions ••
Cut 2 red onions, 2 red peppers, 3-4 scotch bonnets and 4 tomatoes. Blend 1 red onion, 2 red peppers, 3-4 scotch bonnets and 4 tomatoes. Add a quarter cup of water into the blender. Sauté the other red onion with oil and add tomato purée until it thickens and darkens. Pour in your blended sauce and keep stirring every 5-10 minutes. Add your seasonings and mix well. Wash your rice thoroughly until the water is clear. Pour the rice in and keep mixing every 5-10 minutes for the first 20 minutes until the sauce and the rice have mixed together. Put foil on top and when the rice is almost cooked, add some butter. It is the final touch that I forgot to film but it just does something sweet to your rice!

Enjoy

Cosy days in. ☁️ ~ this is a very strange time in humanity but I thought I’d share some tips to those of you who are finding it hard to adjust to being indoors all day. You may find it difficult to be still because we are all so used to working that we don’t know how to relax our minds. I like to always let light into my home in the mornings. I always open my window(s) to let fresh air in as well as making my bed so I’m less tempted to get back in. I always play Lo-fi beats as they relax me and the lyrics don’t distract me from my own thoughts. Lighting a candle or burning incense is a great way to calm your space too. Set yourself a simple task whether it’s reading a new book, doing laundry, spending 15 minutes meditating, watching a series, journaling, doing 10 minutes worth of eMails or just sitting down. Our minds find comfort in accomplishment but it doesn’t have to be anything over the top. This is a great time to make peace with things you were too busy to. Have you forgiven lately? Or said your apology? And if you are still on your hustle, stay safe and avoid any contact with people; don’t feel bad for creating boundaries or politely saying no if someone tries to hug you or shake your hand. You have to look out for yourself and your health. I wish you all peace during this time! I’ve created my safe space at home and I’ve set my boundaries, it’s time for you to do yours. #niaTHELIGHT shot on film by @dazhaneleahphotos

As I stood here and took this picture, I realised I was representing for so many women beyond me. Women who have natural hair, women who are African, British, Caribbean, biracial, women who have acne and women who have stretch marks. The moral of the story, always live in your truth. Hair Tip Time! 
1. Always sleep on a satin pillow! I always tie my hair in a pineapple but sometimes I get lazy and sleep with it all out. 
2. Make sure you always smooth down conditioner on your ends. It's the oldest part of your hair.
3. Detangle starting from your ends and work your way up so you don't rip your hair. I like to use my fingers first then smooth it with the @LovingYourHair brush! 
4. Apply product on fully wet hair and once it is air drying, do not touch it to prevent frizz. 
5. Rake your product through to moisturise the hair then scrunch for that extra definition. 
On this wash day I used @LottaBodyUK Curl & Style milk! I followed the same method I always do.
